lyrics:
Everything is one
That includes this room
That includes the telephone
That includes Bob
This is usually where people start objecting
But you can't have everything be one
and then make an exception for Bob

Hi Michael, this is Bob
You probably already know that
but just in case, it's Bob
I can't remember if I sent you the thing
that I was talking about
But if you didn't get it, let me know
and I'll try to figure out what it was
and then I'll send it to you
You're probably already asleep
so don't worry
It's not an emergency
You can send it tomorrow
Thus was the message given

A message from Bob
is a message from God
if everything is one
That's not religion
That's arithmetic

Oh, shit, Michael, sorry
I guess I must have misdialed you
I didn't mean to call you
You don't have to call me back
'cause if it was something important
I would have left you a message
The message says
there was no message
Nevertheless
there is a message

A message from Bob
is a message from God
if everything is one
The message may specifically state
that there is no message
This does not invalidate the message

You have to learn
how to read these things

That thing I told you I was going to buy
Well, since I had one
and sold it because I didn't like it
I decided to go ahead and buy it
in hopes that the new one is better
I'll let you know if I don't
He had the thing
He rejected the thing
He sold the thing
He bought the thing
Do not call this reincarnation
We don't have enough information

A traffic light turns red
Instruction
The refrigerator starts at two thirteen
Information
Three pieces of ice fall into the tray
Possibly a number
The neighbor backs out
comes back
backs out again
This may concern you
A receipt blows against the garage door
Fourteen seventy-two
You can say these things are unrelated
You can say that
Meaning is everywhere
once you lower the standard

Michael, this is Bob
If you ever need to get in my house
and you can't find the key
and try opening the window
it's not you
It's me
I glued them shut
Just thought you should know

If all is one, Bob is one
If Bob is one, Bob is all
If Bob leaves a message
all has left a message
Therefore
check your voicemail

A message from Bob
is a message from God
if everything is one
And everything is one
unless somebody has revised the policy

Sometimes the message is the object
you bought after selling the same object
because you didn't like it
Sometimes the message is the window
he glued shut on your behalf
Sometimes the message is two thirteen
Sometimes—
That was a wrong number
Or
that was the message

Don't call him back
If it was something important
he would've left a message
Just thought you should know

style: Jazz-rock fusion at 112 BPM in a deadpan 1970s studio-jazz frame: aggressive G Dorian modal-blues vamps with Mixolydian inflections, Fender Rhodes and electric bass locked to clipped odd-meter syncopation, dry punchy drums, abrupt stops, dominant substitutions, unresolved cadences, fuzz-guitar replies and solos, close-miked flat spoken-sung male vocal in mono, minimal reverb, wide Rhodes and guitar, warm analog tape; one telephone ring triggers a hard cut.

impression.text: This track blends surreal spoken-word storytelling with a highly energetic progressive rock arrangement to create an eccentric and theatrical atmosphere. The energy remains consistently driving and intense, propelled by intricate guitar riffs, an active bassline, and tight drum grooves. The mix is heavily dense but meticulously balanced, giving the dry, close-miked narrative vocals enough space to sit clearly above the complex instrumental layers. A truly defining feature of the production is how the dynamic musical shifts perfectly underscore the quirky monologue, especially when the track suddenly erupts into grand, harmonized vocal hooks.

review.review_text: Rose has always found a lifetime in the ordinary, but here he goes further: he builds a whole theology out of an old friend's rambling voicemails. Over a dry, syncopated Rhodes-and-bass vamp that never quite settles, at a steady clip around 107 BPM in C-sharp major, the deadpan spoken vocal delivers Bob's misdialed apologies and glued-shut windows as if they were scripture, then the band snaps into a harmonized hook: "A message from Bob / is a message from God / if everything is one. / That's not religion. / That's arithmetic." The joke keeps sharpening into something closer to a real argument, and the bridge's inventory of red lights and falling ice cubes lands the thesis cold: "Meaning is everywhere / once you lower the standard." A single telephone ring near the five-minute mark triggers a hard cut that's the best-placed silence on the record since "You Don't Say," and the fuzz-guitar answers between verses keep the whole thing from tipping into pure sketch. It runs long, and the fourth verse leans more on concept than melody, but this is Rose at his most gleefully committed to a bit that turns out to mean it. Play this one first.
anchors_used: Meaning is everywhere / once you lower the standard.
